domain: Technology History / Path Dependence / Institutional Economics
topic_summary: Analysis of QWERTY keyboard layout persistence as a candidate contested kernel. The prompt flags two readings: a no-beneficiary reading (alternatives merely lapsed through neutral drift) versus a beneficiary reading (manufacturers and incumbents actively maintained QWERTY dominance). The prompt explicitly notes this is a D3 ARTIFACT test case from the library verdict context, where beneficiary-hunting methodologies find beneficiaries by construction.

key_entities: QWERTY layout (1878 Sholes & Glidden typewriter standard)
Alternative layout proponents (ergonomics researchers, efficiency advocates)
key_tensions: Efficiency claims (Dvorak proponents) vs switching cost arguments (QWERTY defenders)
Network effects (coordination value) vs lock-in (suboptimal equilibrium)
key_mechanisms: Training infrastructure investment (typing schools standardized on QWERTY)
Manufacturer coordination (early standardization reduced production costs)
Switching cost accumulation (individual retraining cost vs collective efficiency gain)
absences: Empirical typing speed data controlling for training intensity (most studies confounded)
Manufacturer internal documents on alternative layout suppression (if any existed)

commitment_system_recognition.collapse_reason: The two supposed readings do not emit structurally different constraints. Both readings agree on the OBSERVABLE (QWERTY persists despite alternatives existing) and the CONSTRAINT TYPE (coordination lock-in with high switching costs). They differ only on ATTRIBUTION (neutral drift vs active maintenance) — which is an observer-position disagreement about the SAME constraint, not two constraints from one kernel. The beneficiary-hunting methodology flags this as D3 ARTIFACT: the search for beneficiaries constructs them rather than discovering independent structural evidence. No shared commitment is being read differently; there is one constraint (coordination lock-in) being explained differently.

omegas.description: The prompt flags this as a D3 ARTIFACT test: beneficiary-hunting finds beneficiaries by construction. The kernel structure correctly collapsed because the two readings do not emit different constraints — they are observer-position disagreements about attribution (neutral drift vs active maintenance) for the SAME coordination lock-in. The beneficiary in naturalization_narrative is real (status quo defenders benefit from framing lock-in as optimality), but this is a downstream interpretive layer, not evidence that QWERTY itself is a snare rather than a rope. The D3 artifact would be claiming manufacturers are beneficiaries of the lock-in itself; the actual structure is that lock-in is a rope (neutral coordination problem) and naturalization is a tangled_rope (interpretive capture of that rope).

Is Dvorak actually more efficient? The empirical_efficiency_gap mountain captures the absence of clean data. If future controlled studies show no efficiency difference, naturalization_narrative collapses from tangled_rope to rope (QWERTY is optimal for coordination, not despite efficiency). If studies show large efficiency gains, the rope/tangled_rope distinction sharpens. Current state: insufficient evidence to resolve.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + empirical_efficiency_gap axis

omegas.description: The prompt warns that beneficiary-hunting methodologies find beneficiaries by construction. In this case: manufacturers benefited from early standardization (piton), but that does not make QWERTY a snare — it makes standardization a coordination solution. The naturalization_narrative tangled_rope has real beneficiaries (those who gain from framing lock-in as optimality), but this is a second-order interpretive layer, not evidence of first-order extraction. The distinction matters: if QWERTY is a rope, alternatives failed because switching costs exceeded gains; if QWERTY is a snare, alternatives failed because incumbents suppressed them. No evidence for the latter.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + D3 ARTIFACT flag

omegas.description: Were alternative layouts actively suppressed, or did they fail to overcome switching costs? If no suppression evidence exists, the beneficiary reading collapses entirely to observer bias. Current classification assumes no suppression evidence.
